verdict.rationale: Riveter documents some first-party control over when results come back. A synchronous quick_search is offered alongside the slower AI-researched search_agent. Async runs can be retrieved via a `wait` long-poll, polling until finished (wait_for_result), or a webhook POST on completion. However, nothing documents an explicit knob for returning partial or incomplete results earlier, or for setting exactly when content is returned. missing for 10: an explicit wait/timeout parameter with documented semantics, early return of partial results, a documented latency-vs-completeness tradeoff, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can trade off latency against completeness by controlling exactly when content is returned

citations.quote: A quick_search lets you quickly web search a query, and pull structured results with urls, titles, and snippets — synchronously, in one request.
A search_agent call asks one question and gets one AI-researched answer back
the SDKs handle auth, retries (429s and transient GET failures), the `wait` long-poll, polling until a run finishes (`wait_for_result`), and pagination
Prefer webhooks over polling: pass `webhook_url` on kickoff and Riveter POSTs the results to you when the run finishes.
